إيران مباشر.. ترمب يرفض مقترح فتح هرمز وطهران تنتظر ردا نهائيا من الوسطاء. رفض الرئيس ترمب المقترح الإيراني لفتح مضيق هرمز وقال إن طهران تريد إعادة فتحه فورا لأنها تتكبد خسائر فادحة، في حين قال وزير الخارجية الإيراني عباس عراقجي إن بلاده بانتظار الموقف النهائي من الوسطاء.

اليمن مباشر.. مباحثات بالرياض لرفع جاهزية القوات اليمنية على وقع تصاعد المعارك. يتواصل التصعيد العسكري بين القوات الحكومية والحوثيين، إذ شهد أمس السبت معارك وغارات وقصفا متبادلا في أكثر من جبهة، بالتزامن مع مباحثات سعودية يمنية في الرياض لرفع القدرات القتالية للقوات اليمنية.

إثيوبيا.. معارك بين عفر وتيغراي تهدد بتوسيع رقعة الصراع. مواجهات بين قوات عفر وجبهة تيغراي تمتد على جبهة واسعة شمال شرقي إثيوبيا، وسط حصار مدينة أبعالا ومخاوف من اتساع آثار القتال على التجارة في المنطقة.

إصابة في اللحظات الأخيرة.. نجم برشلونة أول مصابي إسبانيا في التوقف الدولي. تعرض إريك غارسيا لإصابة خلال الإحماء قبل مواجهة إسبانيا وإنجلترا في دوري الأمم الأوروبية، ليخرج من التشكيلة الأساسية في اللحظات الأخيرة ويحل مارك بوبيل بدلا منه.

خريطة تفاعلية للمعارك في إثيوبيا.. عفر بين تيغراي وطريق جيبوتي. تتسارع المعارك شمالي إثيوبيا في المثلث الحدودي بين تيغراي وعفر وأمهرة، وسط صراع على ألاماتا ومساع لقطع طريق الإمداد الحيوي الذي يربط العمق الإثيوبي بميناء جيبوتي.

تضاعفت مقاعده أربع مرات.. لماذا اصطف العدالة والتنمية في المعارضة؟. حسب النتائج النهائية التي أعلنتها وزارة الداخلية، حصل حزب العدالة والتنمية على 54 مقعدا، مضاعِفا استحقاقه 4 مرات، وقرر مجلسه الوطني الاصطفاف في المعارضة قبل حسم مشاورات تشكيل الحكومة.
ليفربول.. مسيرة حاشدة تطالب بوقف تسليح إسرائيل. مسيرة حاشدة في ليفربول تطالب حكومة حزب العمال بوقف تصدير الأسلحة إلى إسرائيل وفرض عقوبات عليها، بالتزامن مع انعقاد مؤتمر الحزب السنوي في المدينة.

نجم برشلونة يكشف عن رغبته في زيارة طبيب نفسي ويعترف بزيادة الضغوط. كشف غافي لاعب برشلونة رغبته في زيارة اختصاصي نفسي للمرة الأولى، معترفا بأن الضغوط التي يعيشها اليوم أكبر من بداياته، وأن الإصابات غيّرت نظرته لكرة القدم وطريقة تعامله مع جسده.
موعد مباراة فرنسا وبلجيكا في دوري الأمم الأوروبية والقنوات الناقلة. نستعرض تفاصيل موعد القمة البلجيكية الفرنسية في دوري الأمم الأوروبية.

إسبانيا تحسم قمة ويمبلي وسباعية لفنلندا.. حصاد دوري الأمم الأوروبية. حسمت إسبانيا قمة ويمبلي بفوز مثير على إنجلترا 3-2، وانتصرت كرواتيا وسويسرا، بينما سجلت فنلندا أكبر نتائج السبت بسباعية في سان مارينو ضمن ختام الجولة الأولى من دوري الأمم الأوروبية.

أسلحة ذاتية التشغيل قد تقتل مليار إنسان؟ خبير يوضح حدود الخطر. تُجدّد المحادثات في جنيف الجدل حول الأسلحة ذاتية التشغيل، بين دعوات أممية لقواعد ملزمة وتحفظ أمريكي روسي، وخبير يستبعد سيناريو قتل مليار إنسان في وضعها الراهن.
موعد مباراة السعودية والعراق في خليجي 27 والقنوات الناقلة. نستعرض تفاصيل القمة الخليجية بين السعودية والعراق في الجولة الحاسمة من دور المجموعات.
موعد مباراة عُمان والكويت في "خليجي 27" والقنوات الناقلة. نستعرض تفاصيل وموعد المواجهة الحاسمة بين عُمان والكويت في خليجي 27.

انسحاب الوفود قبل كلمة نتنياهو.. دانون يشكك في المشهد وفيدان يؤكد عزلة إسرائيل. وصف مندوب إسرائيل بالأمم المتحدة انسحاب الوفود أثناء كلمة نتنياهو بـ"المشهد الإعلامي المضلل"، مدعيا أن خروج المندوبين جرى ترتيبه مسبقا لإحداث ضجة، بينما أكد وزير خارجية تركيا أن عزلة إسرائيل تتزايد.

لافروف يطلق مبادرة لتسوية أزمة هرمز ويلتقي نظيره الألماني بعد انقطاع. أعلن وزير الخارجية الروسي سيرغي لافروف مبادرة لإرساء السلام في الخليج وتسوية أزمة هرمز، بالتزامن مع لقاء جمعه بوزير الخارجية الألماني يوهان فاديفول، هو الأول من نوعه منذ عام 2022.

المعارضة الإسرائيلية توحّد صفوفها لإسقاط نتنياهو. اتفق قادة 5 أحزاب معارضة إسرائيلية على تنسيق جهودهم استعدادا لانتخابات 27 أكتوبر/تشرين الأول، بهدف تعزيز فرصهم في تشكيل الحكومة المقبلة بدل حكومة بنيامين نتنياهو.

التشابه المريب.. هل سرق فيبر إنجازات البيروني الفكرية؟. يتناول المقال التشابه بين دراسات البيروني وفيبر لنظام الطبقات في الهند، متسائلا عن احتمال استفادة فيبر من البيروني دون الإشارة إليه، وداعيا إلى إعادة فحص مصادر علم الاجتماع غير الغربية في تأسيسه.

"العنكبوت الكولومبي" في قبضة الأمن الأمريكي. سلمت السلطات الكولومبية جيوفاني أندريس روخاس زعيم حركة "كوماندوس دي لا فرونتيرا" المتمردة إلى الولايات المتحدة، بعد أن تأخر تسليمه عدة أشهر بسبب منحه حصانة من قبل الحكومة الكولومبية السابقة.

وول ستريت جورنال: وزارة الخزانة خيرت دولا بين العقوبات والتعامل مع طهران. ذكرت صحيفة وول ستريت جورنال أن واشنطن خيّرت شركاء إيران التجاريين بين التعامل مع طهران والحفاظ على علاقاتهم الاقتصادية مع واشنطن، في حملة ضغط تستهدف خنق ما تبقى من قنواتها المالية والجوية.

قضية المسنة ماريكار تشعل شوارع مدريد ضد أزمة السكن. تظاهر عشرات الآلاف في مدريد احتجاجا على أزمة السكن، بعد طرد امرأة تبلغ 87 عاما من شقتها التي عاشت فيها عقودا، وسط مطالب بحماية المستأجرين وفرض قيود على الإخلاءات وارتفاع الإيجارات.
سموتريتش يدعو لشن حرب وتفكيك السلطة بالضفة. طالب وزير المالية الإسرائيلي المتطرف بتسلئيل سموتريتش بشن حرب واسعة في الضفة الغربية وتفكيك السلطة الفلسطينية.

السويسريون يصوتون على تشديد حيادهم التاريخي. بين يمين يرفع شعار "الحياد المسلح والدائم" وحكومة تحذر من جمود يقيّد الحركة، يتوجه السويسريون إلى استفتاء قد تُفهم نتيجته بـ"لا" خارج الحدود كأنهم يطوون صفحة حيادهم العتيق.
شاهد البث المباشر لتلفزيون بي بي سي
هل تؤثر مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي على علاقاتنا العاطفية؟. هل تؤثر مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي والمحتوى الذي نستهلكه عن العلاقات العاطفية في الطريقة التي نعيش بها علاقاتنا؟
صور تُظهر أضراراً واسعة في مواقع أمريكية بدول عربية جرّاء هجمات إيرانية. طائرة عسكرية محطمة ومبانٍ مدمرة تظهر في صور حصلت عليها شبكة "سي بي إس نيوز"، الشريك الأمريكي لبي بي سي.

عبد الملك الحوثي.. من هو زعيم حركة "أنصار الله" في اليمن؟. يلعب عبد الملك الحوثي، زعيم جماعة أنصار الله الحوثية، دوراً بارزاً في الحياة السياسية في اليمن. فماذا نعرف عنه؟ وما أبرز الصراعات التي انخرطت فيها الحركة تحت زعامته؟

باب المندب: كيف وصل الحوثيون إلى مكمن الضعف الإستراتيجي للسعودية؟. الهجوم الحوثي الأخير، الذي أسفر عن السيطرة على معظم الساحل الغربي لليمن المطل على البحر الأحمر والتقدم حتى مضيق باب المندب، ربما منح طهران أوراق ضغط أكبر في مواجهة واشنطن. إلا أنه يكشف أيضاً عن تنامي القدرات العسكرية والتنظيمية للجماعة نفسها، وعن المعضلة شديدة التعقيد التي تواجهها السعودية، التي تعاني أصلاً من استنزاف مواردها وتعدد التحديات التي تواجهها.

أمجد فريد في بلا قيود: اتهام أمريكا للجيش السوداني باستخدام أسلحة كيماوية في غير محله. شدّد الدكتور أمجد فريد مستشار مجلس السيادة السوداني للشؤون السياسية والعلاقات الخارجية على وجود آلية لمحاكمة من يرتكب جريمة أو انتهاكا من قِبل أي من جنود وضباط القوات المسلحة السودانية أوالقوات الموالية لها وخضوعهم أمام محاكم عسكرية أو مدنية أو إحالتهم إلى التقاعد.
لماذا تنخفض نتائج اختبارات جيل زد؟. كشفت أكبر دراسة دولية في العالم تُجرى على مراهقين في الخامسة عشرة من العمر عن انخفاض مُقلق في نتائج العلوم والرياضيات والقراءة.

هل تتدخل تركيا وباكستان لحماية السعودية أمام هجمات الحوثيين؟. مع تصاعد التوترات بين السعودية والحوثيين، واستمرار الهجمات على مدن السعودية، تطرح التساؤلات حول دور "حلف مكة" في مساعدة السعودية ضد حركة أنصار الله الحوثية، فما هو موقف تركيا وباكستان من التصعيد؟

لماذا يسعى السودانيون لاستخراج الذهب رغم المخاطر العالية؟. في ظل الأزمة الاقتصادية وتراجع مصادر الدخل، يتجه كثير من السودانيين إلى استخراج الذهب باعتباره فرصة سريعة لكسب المال وتأمين لقمة العيش، رغم المخاطر.

هل يمكن للعقوبات الأمريكية أن تغلق الباب أمام الرحلات الجوية الأجنبية إلى إيران؟. بينما توقفت فعلياً رحلات شركات الطيران الأجنبية إلى إيران عقب الحرب والتوترات الإقليمية، فرضت الولايات المتحدة عقوبات جديدة على قطاع الطيران الإيراني قد تجعل عودة هذه الرحلات أكثر تعقيداً وصعوبة، حتى بعد انحسار المخاطر الأمنية.

الذكاء الاصطناعي ونهاية الزمان: لماذا يعتقد بعض الناس أن هذه التكنولوجيا هي المسيح الدجال؟. بدأ العديد من المسيحيين البارزين، عبر منصات تتراوح بين تيك توك والبودكاست وقطاع النشر، مناقشة ما إذا كان الذكاء الاصطناعي يمكن أن يكون عاملاً محفزاً لدمار العالم.
كيف يساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي على إدارة تخزين واستهلاك الكهرباء في المنزل؟
ما الفرق بين المملكة المتحدة وإنجلترا وبريطانيا؟. المملكة المتحدة تضم أربع دول، إنجلترا وويلز وإسكتلندا وأيرلندا الشمالية، وهذه بعض أبرز المعلومات عنها.

كيف أصبحت المسيرات قادرة على استهداف بعضها؟. أعلن الجيش السوداني مؤخرا عن عدة عمليات إسقاط لطائرات مسيرة صينية الصنع مملوكة لقوات الدعم السريع عبر صواريخ جو - جو أطلقت من مسيرات يملكها الجيش. فماذا نعرف عن تقنيات اعتراض الطائرات المسيرة؟ ولماذا يعد ما حدث في السودان تاريخيا؟

"إهانة نتنياهو في الأمم المتحدة تشي بأن أيامه باتت معدودة" - مقال في الإندبندنت. في جولة الصحف البريطانية اليوم تعليق للإندبندنت حول "إهانة" نتنياهو في الأمم المتحدة بمغادرة وفود دبلوماسية أثناء إلقاء كلمته، ورأي في الغارديان حول بداية تحدي سياسات ترامب من بعض الدول.

البيت الأبيض يمنع "سي إن إن" من مرافقة ترامب على متن الطائرة الرئاسية "إير فورس وان". في خطوة هي الأحدث في المواجهة بين البيت الأبيض ووسائل الإعلام، مُنعت شبكة "سي إن إن" الأمريكية من مرافقة الرئيس دونالد ترامب على متن الطائرة الرئاسية "إير فورس وان" خلال رحلته إلى ولاية تينيسي يوم السبت.

مقتل 11 شخصاً في هجوم بسيارة مفخخة استهدف نقطة أمنية شمال غربي باكستان. لم تعلن أي جهة مسؤوليتها عن الهجوم حتى الآن، فيما يأتي بعد يومين من إعلان باكستان تنفيذ ضربات جوية ضد مسلحين مشتبه بهم في أفغانستان.

انقطاع الإنترنت والاتصالات في تيغراي وسط مخاوف حيال عودة الحرب الإثيوبية. اشتباكات بين الجبهة الشعبية لتحرير تيغراي، والحكومة تقطع الاتصالات عن أجزاء كبيرة من الإقليم وسط مخاوف من عودة الحرب مرة أخرى.
بعد تصويت اللاعبين، أيرلندا تخوض مباراتها أمام إسرائيل. أيرلندا تقبل خوض مباراة أمام إسرائيل في دوري الأمم الأوروبية بعد سجال بين الجانبين ودراسة لاعبين أيرلنديين مقاطعة المباراة.
العثور على جثة امرأة عاشرة في جنوب أفريقيا وسط تحقيقات للشرطة في جرائم القتل. أثارت هذه الوفيات موجة استنكار على مستوى البلاد بشأن حجم العنف ضد النساء فيها.

قضايا الشرق الأوسط وأزمة هرمز تتصدر خطابات اليوم الخامس للجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة. تتواصل في مقر الأمم المتحدة في نيويورك أعمال المناقشة العامة للدورة الـ81 للجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة، التي افتتحت الثلاثاء 22 سبتمبر/أيلول، وتختتم الاثنين 28 سبتمبر/ أيلول 2026.

"الإصلاح ممكن": ما الذي يساعدنا حقاً في إنقاذ علاقاتنا؟. هل يمكن إنقاذ علاقة تتجه نحو الانهيار؟ خبراء العلاج الزوجي يقولون إن الأمر ممكن. من الخلافات المتكررة حول المال والأعمال المنزلية إلى السلوكيات الأربع التي قد "تقتل" العلاقة، تكشف الأبحاث ما يميز الأزواج السعداء عن غير السعداء.

ترامب يرفض مقترح إيران بشأن هرمز، وطهران تنتظر موقف واشنطن النهائي عبر الوسطاء. أكد بزشكيان أن بنود الاتفاق الجديد الذي اقترحته طهران لإعادة فتح مضيق هرمز الاستراتيجي وُضعت "بالتنسيق" مع المرشد الأعلى وسيتم تنفيذها "دون أي مشاكل" إذا وافقت الولايات المتحدة.

Une situation qui pousse les armateurs à repenser leurs trajets, sans pour autant automatiser le passage par le cap de Bonne-Espérance.

Maroc : dans l’attente du choix du chef du gouvernement, les alliances prennent forme. Si le PAM est arrivé nettement en tête des législatives du 23 septembre, les résultats ne permettent pas encore de déterminer quels partis formeront une coalition pour gouverner. Revigoré par son score, le PJD annonce déjà son intention de faire tomber le prochain exécutif.

Minerais critiques : Washington accélère son offensive stratégique au Nigeria. Le Nigeria et les États-Unis ont signé un accord-cadre pour développer les ressources minérales nigérianes, estimées à 700 milliards de dollars. Un partenariat qui s’inscrit dans la rivalité croissante entre Washington et Pékin sur le continent.

Guerre en Éthiopie : la nouvelle rébellion du Tigré est-elle en mesure de menacer la capitale ?. Le nord de l’Éthiopie s’embrase à nouveau. TPLF, Fano et OLA, jadis ennemis, ont formé une alliance inédite pour renverser le gouvernement d’Abiy Ahmed.

Jeremy Awori (Ecobank) : « Là où nous sommes plus petits, une acquisition est le moyen le plus rapide de grandir ». Ecobank fête ses quarante ans avec des résultats au plus haut et un capital qui change de mains. Son directeur général révèle les ambitions nouvelles de la plus panafricaine des banques.

Pourquoi Dangote mise 660 millions de dollars sur un oléoduc entre Djibouti et l’Éthiopie. Une conduite de 120 km reliera Damerjog, à Djibouti, à Dewele, en Éthiopie. Objectif : réduire les coûts et les délais d’approvisionnement en carburant du deuxième pays le plus peuplé d’Afrique.

Dette du Sénégal : les banques régionales peuvent-elles éviter la restructuration de leurs créances ?. Dans une analyse, S&P juge les grandes banques africaines à l’abri du plan de restructuration de la dette sénégalaise. Mais l’exclusion de la dette en francs CFA n’est pas garantie, et les établissements ivoiriens sont particulièrement exposés.

Terrorisme, dette et Macky Sall : ce qu’il faut retenir de la venue à l’ONU de Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Le président sénégalais a réaffirmé son soutien à la candidature de son prédécesseur au secrétariat général des Nations unies, accentuant encore la fracture avec son ex-Premier ministre, Ousmane Sonko. Il a également lancé un appel à un sursaut face à la propagation de la violence jihadiste au Sahel.

En Côte d’Ivoire, Tidjane Thiam peut-il survivre à ses procès ?. Le verdict du 22 octobre approche, mais une nouvelle assignation vise déjà le patron du PDCI. Entre bataille judiciaire, tensions internes et stratégie d’apaisement, le parti, qui célèbre ses 80 ans, doit prouver qu’il peut résister à ses propres fractures.

RDC : ce que l’on sait du crash qui a coûté la vie à l’auditeur général des FARDC. Dix-sept personnes, dont plusieurs officiers de l’armée congolaise, ont péri le 25 septembre dans le crash d’un avion. Plusieurs sources ont confirmé à Jeune Afrique la présence de l’auditeur général des forces armées, le général Lucien-René Likulia Bakumi, parmi les victimes.

En Centrafrique, la guerre des prérogatives autour de Faustin-Archange Touadéra. Finances publiques, grands travaux, sécurité, diplomatie… À Bangui, les rivalités entre les conseillers présidentiels et les ministres se multiplient. Une guerre d’influence qui entrave l’action publique et brouille les circuits de décision.

Air Sénégal sous perfusion, tractations politiques au Maroc, offensive chinoise sur le lithium africain… Les 5 infos qu’il ne fallait pas manquer. Cette semaine, le Brief de Jeune Afrique revient sur l’opération de sauvetage d’Air Sénégal, tire les enseignements des élections législatives au Maroc, décrypte l’architecture du pouvoir ivoirien, évalue le poids de l’opposition en RDC et constate la main mise de la Chine sur le lithium africain.

Guinée : Sidya Touré, l’ex-Premier ministre devenu opposant éternel, est mort en exil. Premier ministre sous Lansana Conté, devenu opposant à Alpha Condé puis à Mamadi Doumbouya, Sidya Touré est mort ce vendredi 25 septembre à Paris, à l’âge de 81 ans. En exil en Côte d’Ivoire depuis 2022, il souhaitait finir ses jours en Guinée.

Côte d’Ivoire : ces femmes qui font l’économie. Pétrole, mines, télécoms… De plus en plus de femmes sont aux manettes dans des secteurs économiques de premier plan en Côte d’Ivoire. Avec la performance, l’innovation et l’ambition comme mots d’ordre.

Comment le Rassemblement national tente de se constituer des réseaux dans le monde arabe. Convaincus d’arriver au pouvoir en 2027, Marine Le Pen et Jordan Bardella, conscients qu’il leur faudrait alors dialoguer avec tous les pays, cherchent des interlocuteurs au Maghreb et au Moyen-Orient. Des régions où le RN, même si on ne le considère toujours pas comme un parti comme les autres, est observé avec intérêt.

Ensemencer les nuages pour les faire pleuvoir : solution miracle ou mirage ?. Faire pleuvoir les nuages, ce n’est pas de la science-fiction. Utilisée en Afrique depuis plusieurs décennies, cette technique ne s’y est pourtant jamais vraiment imposée. Mais la multiplication des sécheresses pourrait la remettre au goût du jour. Avec quels résultats ? Réponse en infographies.

JOJ de Dakar 2026 : le Sénégal dans les starting-blocks. Sécurité, logistique, transports, hébergement… À quelques semaines du coup d’envoi des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (31 octobre-13 novembre) – la première compétition olympique organisée sur le sol africain –, la capitale sénégalaise, ville hôte, est dans la dernière ligne droite des préparatifs.

Cameroun : « Le contrôle de la DGRE est un enjeu crucial pour les différents clans autour de Paul Biya ». Le service de renseignements camerounais, déjà le théâtre de rivalités politiques entre des clans ennemis autour du chef de l’État, est devenu un réel bazar aux informations confidentielles, accessibles au plus offrant.

En Ethiopie, les rebelles du Tigré disent repousser une « invasion » des forces fédérales. Les Forces de défense tigréennes ont, par ailleurs, pris le contrôle de l’aéroport de Makalé, capitale de l’Etat. Trois jours plus tôt, sept mouvements actifs dans différentes régions du pays avaient annoncé la création d’une alliance pour renverser les autorités fédérales.

Au Mali, l’amertume des militaires en première ligne contre les djihadistes. Le 10 septembre, l’armée malienne a subi l’un de ses pires revers : au moins 100 soldats sont morts dans l’attaque du camp de Dioura par le GSIM. Une défaite qui met à nouveau sous pression le chef de la junte.

« Il faut être motivé pour voter » : au Maroc, les élections législatives sous la menace d’une abstention élevée. Le taux de participation est l’enjeu majeur du scrutin de mercredi, alors que la coalition gouvernementale sortante cherche à conforter sa majorité.

Rwanda et Belgique aplanissent leur différend sur la guerre en RDC et scellent leur réconciliation. En marge de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, Bruxelles et Kigali ont annoncé rétablir leurs relations diplomatiques, dix-huit mois après une rupture décidée par le Rwanda, qui accusait la Belgique de prendre parti contre lui dans le conflit qui ravage l’est de la République démocratique du Congo.

En Ethiopie, après le déclenchement d’offensives par plusieurs groupes rebelles, le pays au bord de la « guerre totale ». Le Front populaire de libération du Tigré et ses alliés ont ciblé des positions contrôlées par l’armée fédérale éthiopienne dans les régions du nord du pays. L’Union africaine et l’Union européenne ont appelé, mercredi, « à la désescalade immédiate ».

Elections législatives au Maroc : la coalition sortante vainqueure d’un scrutin au taux de participation d’à peine 38 %. Ce taux de participation est le plus bas depuis près de vingt ans. Sans majorité absolue, le Parti Authenticité et modernité (PAM) devra former une nouvelle alliance avec les autres partis.

Entre l’Afrique du Sud et les Etats-Unis, le bras de fer diplomatique reprend. L’administration Trump a confirmé, mardi, sa volonté de privilégier les Afrikaners, des Blancs d’Afrique du Sud, dans l’accès au droit d’asile. Une mesure perçue comme une humiliation par le Congrès national africain, le parti du président sud-africain.

En Afrique du Sud, des voix s’élèvent chez les Afrikaaners pour refuser les faveurs de Donald Trump. L’association Afrikaners vir Suid Afrika rejette « le discours qui dépeint les Afrikaners comme des victimes de persécution raciale dans l’Afrique du Sud post-apartheid ». Des propos qui murmurent aux oreilles du camp MAGA.

Au Nigeria, la mort de 37 orpailleurs en détention pèse sur la campagne présidentielle. Dans le centre du pays, 37 jeunes mineurs sont morts dans une cellule surchauffée et surpeuplée alors qu’ils étaient détenus par une unité des forces de sécurité, le 17 septembre. A l’approche de l’élection présidentielle, les autorités réagissent avec une détermination inhabituelle.

Les leçons des législatives au Maroc : recomposition au sein de la coalition gouvernementale, retour des islamistes et abstention massive. A l’issue du scrutin du 23 septembre, le Parti Authenticité et modernité s’impose comme la première force politique du pays. Des tractations vont débuter pour former une majorité gouvernementale, avant l’ouverture de la législature fixée au 9 octobre.

Au Maghreb, le danger d’une dévitalisation des partis politiques. La faible participation aux élections législatives marocaines du 23 septembre illustre une désaffection de l’offre partisane, également observable en Algérie et en Tunisie. Dans tout le Maghreb, les partis sont en crise, victimes d’une panne de projets mais aussi des stratégies d’affaiblissement menées par les régimes en place.

La Côte d’Ivoire se donne six mois pour éradiquer l’orpaillage clandestin. En pleine flambée du cours de l’or, l’Etat ouest-africain veut endiguer le manque à gagner fiscal mais aussi des pratiques dangereuses sur les plans sanitaire et environnemental, notamment dans l’usage du mercure. Cette économie informelle est toutefois un « vecteur de paix sociale » dans des zones déshéritées, dont les terres ont été épuisées par l’agriculture intensive.

Prise dans les turbulences de la crise au Moyen-Orient, l’économie égyptienne résiste. La fermeture du détroit d’Ormuz et les attaques contre les infrastructures énergétiques régionales renchérissent la facture gazière de l’Egypte et fragilisent plusieurs de ses principales sources de devises. Mais Le Caire tente aussi de tirer parti de sa position géographique pour devenir un carrefour des nouvelles routes commerciales.

L’Ethiopie, géant africain rattrapé par la guerre : qui sont les belligérants, quels sont leurs objectifs ?. La guerre a repris en Ethiopie, géant démographique de la Corne de l’Afrique. Les combats opposent différents groupes rebelles, constitués le plus souvent sur des bases ethniques, à l’armée fédérale. Dans cette mosaïque complexe, les renversements d’alliance sont fréquents.

Au Congo, derrière une opération de lutte contre la criminalité, des centaines de disparitions et des exécutions sommaires. Face à l’expansion d’une délinquance urbaine de plus en plus structurée, les autorités ont lancé l’opération « Zéro kuluna » en septembre 2025. Mais les méthodes employées sont largement décriées.

Au Niger, l’organisation Etat islamique de plus en plus puissante. Au moins une cinquantaine de militaires nigériens ont été tués dans deux attaques menées par le groupe djihadiste mercredi 23 septembre. L’EI étend son influence dans cet Etat du Sahel, et concurrence ses rivaux du Groupe de soutien de l’islam et des musulmans.

CAN 2027 : face aux retards accumulés par les trois pays organisateurs, la Confédération africaine de football envisage des solutions de remplacement. La lenteur des travaux au Kenya, en Ouganda et en Tanzanie fait naître des doutes quant à la capacité de ces pays à organiser la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des nations de football, à l’été 2027. La CAF a sondé plusieurs pays susceptibles d’accueillir la compétition au pied levé.

Législatives au Maroc : « Le vote du monde rural est toujours déterminant ». Lors des élections législatives du 23 septembre, le taux de participation a été le plus faible depuis 2007. Les partis issus de la coalition sortante ont capitalisé sur le vote des ruraux, plus mobilisés que les urbains, souligne le sociologue Zakaria Kadiri dans un entretien au « Monde ».

Le chanteur marocain Saad Lamjarred condamné en appel à dix ans de prison pour viol ; sa peine alourdie. L’artiste veut se pourvoir en cassation, a fait savoir samedi l’une de ses avocates. Il avait été condamné à six ans de réclusion criminelle en première instance.

Afrique, Palestine, Ukraine… L’UE annonce 710 millions d’euros d’aide dans plusieurs régions du monde en crise. Une partie de cette somme, 380 millions d’euros, sera allouée en Afrique subsaharienne pour le financement d’actions liées aux migrations, « axées sur la protection des migrants vulnérables, le soutien au retour volontaire et à la réintégration », selon un communiqué.

At least 16 killed in Russian and Ukrainian strikes. Russian and Ukrainian strikes have killed at least 16 people over the last 24 hours, both countries said Saturday. The attacks have intensified from both sides as the war continues with no diplomatic breakthrough in sight.

Tenth woman found dead in South Africa’s string of killings. Police in South Africa discovered a tenth body in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg, amid a string of killings of women over the past two months. The latest discovery has heightened concerns over violence against women in the country.

Egypt’s Salah ruled out of South Sudan qualifier due to artificial surface. Mohamed Salah will not travel with Egypt’s squad for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against South Sudan because the match will be played on an artificial turf pitch, the Egyptian Football Association announced.

Putellas wants to bring ‘winning culture and mentality’ to London City. Spanish football star Alexia Putellas has left Barcelona after 14 years to join the London City Lionesses, an independent club in England’s Women’s Super League. She aims to bring her winning experience and mentality to the ambitious team.

Houthis forcing children to fight on Yemen’s battlefields, civil society groups warn. German, Russian foreign ministers have rare meeting at UN. The foreign ministers of Germany and Russia held their first known one-on-one meeting since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The German minister reportedly called for de-escalation, while his Russian counterpart later defended the war in a speech.

Karrar Nabeel’s last-second winner gifts Iraq 3-2 win over Kuwait. When Youssef Nasser equalized for Kuwait in the 90th minute, Iraqi fans feared their team had fallen into the same trap as they had against Oman. Roads flood in New Jersey, inundate some homes, as major signs of nor’easter take shape. A powerful nor’easter is causing widespread power outages and flooding in the U.S. Northeast, with coastal communities in New Jersey particularly affected. The storm has prompted warnings of dangerous conditions through the weekend and has led to flight cancellations.

Saudi FM warns the world to take Gulf security seriously. NEW YORK: The world is facing “unprecedented challenges,” Saudi Arabia’s foreign minister told the UN General Assembly on Saturday, as he condemned “flagrant” Iranian and Houthi attacks on his country and warned the world to take Gulf security seriously. Germany ready to ‘walk through fire’ for Klopp, says Tah. Germany defender Jonathan Tah has praised the immediate impact of new national coach Jurgen Klopp, stating the squad is ‘ready to walk through fire’ for him. Klopp took over the team following Germany’s disappointing early exit from the last World Cup.

Gutsy Vollering wins cycling road race world title. Dutch cyclist Demi Vollering has won the women’s road race world title in Montreal, capping off a successful season by finishing ahead of Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney in a record 180km race.

Commanders of Joint Forces, Yemen’s National Resistance Forces discuss ways to support Yemeni army. RIYADH: The Commander of the Joint Forces and the Commander of Yemen’s National Resistance Forces discussed ways to support the readiness of the Yemeni Armed Forces to restore the state and its national institutions on Saturday. Hamas leader says Israel to use Gaza ‘blood’ in election. Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya stated in an interview that he does not expect any meaningful change from Israel’s upcoming election, accusing all Israeli political parties of using the “blood” of Gazans as “fuel” for their campaigns.

BUENOS AIRES: Saudi Ambassador to Argentina Hatem Al-Ghamdi recently met with Argentina’s Secretary of Energy Maria Carmen Tettamanti in Buenos Aires. "When a decision affects an entire school community for a full week, families deserve clear communication and transparency about the reasons behind it," one parent living in Riyadh who spoke on condition of anonymity told AFP. The announcement comes a day after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles targeting the kingdom. The strikes were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks since July, when renewed hostilities shattered a years-long truce and embroiled Yemen in the wider Middle East war. The United Nations Security Council earlier condemned escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi fighters, noting that the strikes have wounded "civilians, including women and children". ATC issues contempt notice to Adiala superintendent over failure to facilitate Imaan, Hadi’s powers of attorney. ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday issued a contempt of court notice to the Adiala jail superintendent for allegedly failing to facilitate the signing and transmission of powers of attorney (vakalatnamas) required to file bail petitions for Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha. On Tuesday, the court returned bail petitions filed by human rights lawyers Imaan and Hadi in the Kohsar police station protest case over the absence of signed powers of attorney. During the proceedings, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra directed the jail superintendent to explain why he should not be sentenced to six months in prison for allegedly disobeying the court’s orders. No representative of Adiala jail appeared before the court, while the two accused could also not be produced through video link despite a previous direction. Dr Shireen Mazari, Imaan’s mother, and a large number of lawyers appeared before the court during the proceedings. The judge expressed displeasure over the failure of the jail authorities to obtain Imaan and Hadi’s signatures on the powers of attorney, which are required to authorise lawyers to represent them in the bail proceedings. Judge Sipra remarked that the jail superintendent should not push the court — or himself — into a corner. He asked whether the deputy superintendent had collected the powers of attorneys from the sessions court on the relevant day. Advocate Riasat Ali Azad told the court that he was not certain whether the documents had been collected from the court. He said the lawyers had submitted the powers of attorneys there for onward transmission to Adiala jail in compliance with the court’s order. The serial numbers of the powers of attorneys submitted to the sessions court were subsequently presented before the bench. The court staff informed Judge Sipra that Imaan and Hadi were not being produced through video link because the jail authorities had cited internet connectivity problems. The judge expressed dissatisfaction with the explanation, observing that the Adiala jail authorities had also repeatedly cited internet connectivity issues in an earlier case. He recalled that he had previously directed experts from PTCL and NTC to visit Adiala jail to resolve the connectivity problem, specifically instructing that experts be sent from Haripur. Judge Sipra observed that obtaining and signing the vakalatnama was a fundamental right of an accused and could not be denied on account of administrative hurdles. The court subsequently issued a show-cause notice for contempt of court to the Adiala jail superintendent and sought an explanation as to why he should not be sentenced to six months’ imprisonment. The ATC adjourned further proceedings until Tuesday. On January 24, an Islamabad sessions court sentenced Imaan and Hadi to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). However, on September 17, the Supreme Court suspended the couple’s sentences in the controversial social media posts case. The SC granted the couple bail against surety bonds of Rs200,000 and ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict. Soon after their release, Islamabad police personnel, led by the SSP Operations, reached Adiala jail and arrested the two again in connection with the Kohsar police station protest case. The police subsequently produced them before the ATC late at night. However, the ATC rejected the police’s request for a 30-day physical remand of the couple and sent them to jail on judicial remand.

Pakistan Navy seizes $750m worth of narcotics in Arabian Sea during joint operation. The Pakistan Navy seized narcotics worth approximately $750 million during a joint counter-narcotics operation in the Arabian Sea, according to a statement issued on Saturday. The operation was conducted by Pakistan Navy ships PNS Hunain and PNS Yarmook under the ambit of maritime security operations, the navy’s Director General Public Relations said. According to the statement, the ships intercepted a suspicious boat during routine patrols and conducted a boarding operation. More than 2,800 kilogrammes of narcotics were recovered from concealed compartments on board the vessel during the subsequent inspection. “This remarkable achievement reflects Pakistan Navy’s sustained surveillance, vigilance, and unwavering commitment to regional maritime security, global peace, and the fight against illicit trafficking at sea.” Following the operation, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf commended the officers and crew of PNS Hunain and PNS Yarmook for their “professionalism, vigilance and dedication”. He said the Pakistan Navy remained committed to safeguarding national maritime interests and maintaining good order at sea while contributing to the security of the global commons. Earlier in June, the navy seized around two tonnes of drugs — 1,500 kilograms of hashish and 500 kgs of ‘ice’ — near the coastline of Gwadar. The value of seized drugs was estimated at around $215 million in the international market. In October last year, the navy seized narcotics worth more than $972 million from sailboats in the Arabian Sea. The navy said in a statement that the achievement highlighted its “unwavering commitment to regional maritime security, global peace, and the collective fight against illicit trafficking at sea”.

'Largest hypocrisy in the world': Pakistan tells UNGA India’s 'terrorist exports' have gone global. Pakistan on Saturday accused India of having “elevated propaganda into statecraft”, embraced disinformation as diplomacy and “exported terrorism as an instrument of policy”, as Islamabad hit back at remarks made by the Indian representative at the UN General Assembly. In a reply to the Indian representative’s statement during the general debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, Counsellor Saima Saleem termed India a state “that has elevated propaganda into statecraft, embraced disinformation as diplomacy, exports terrorism as an instrument of policy, pursues hegemony as a regional strategy, mainstreamed Islamophobia and institutionalised Hindutva ideology”. “The extraordinary balance sheet of today’s incredibly intolerant India. It exports terrorism and violence while trying to import victimhood and sympathy,” she said. “Pakistan knows the cost of Indian-sponsored terrorism all too well,” she said, adding that since the turn of the century, Pakistan had lost nearly 100,000 lives to terrorism, generations had been scarred and billions of dollars had been drained from the country’s economy. She said Pakistan’s counter-terrorism efforts and sacrifices had been well recognised internationally. “We have also presented to the international community extensive evidence of India’s financing, aiding and abetting of terrorist groups targeting Pakistanis, including the TTP, BLA and Majeed Brigade,” she said. “Yet, despite its endless lectures to others on terrorism, we are still waiting to hear India unequivocally condemn the terrorist attacks that kill innocent Pakistani civilians. But how can we expect India to condemn its proxies?” she stated. She said India’s “terrorist exports have gone from regional to global”, citing former Indian naval commander Kulbhushan Jadhav, convicted in Pakistan on terrorism and espionage charges, and Nikhil Gupta, who pleaded guilty in the United States for plotting the murder of a Sikh leader at the direction of the Indian government. She also referred to “others implicated in assassinations carried out in Canada”. Kashmir dispute Turning to the Kashmir dispute, the counsellor said: “Jammu and Kashmir never was, neither is, nor will ever be an integral part of India. It is an internationally recognised disputed territory, a huge part of which is under India’s forcible and illegal occupation for nearly eight decades against the wishes of the Kashmiri people, and in gross violation of international law and numerous resolutions of the Security Council.” “The contrast between AJK and Indian-occupied Jammu and Kashmir could not be more stark,” she said. “In AJK, Kashmiris enjoy rights, participate in political life and have the freedom to express their opinions, while the people of Indian-occupied Kashmir endure decades of occupation, repression and denial of their fundamental rights and freedoms, including the inalienable right to self-determination. Rights exercised cannot be equated with rights denied,” she said. ‘Largest hypocrisy in the world’ Saima said the ruling RSS-BJP dispensation in India had “institutionalised Hindutva ideology in state policy and practice, and unleashed a reign of terror against minorities”. “Muslims are demonised; Christians persecuted; Dalits dehumanised; and Sikhs disenfranchised in the largest hypocrisy in the world,” she said. She said massacres of Muslims in Gujarat and Delhi under state patronage, calls for the genocide of Muslims, Islamophobic rhetoric by politicians and discriminatory citizenship laws were part of the “Hindutva project”. Indus Waters Treaty On the Indus Waters Treaty, Saima said that by the “so-called holding in abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty and blatantly disregarding its international legal obligations, including the sanctity of treaties”, India had “stooped to a new low of weaponising water, a lifeline for the 240 million people of Pakistan”. She said India’s “false narratives and disinformation could not hide the crushing defeat it suffered at Pakistan’s hands during Marka-i-Haq in May 2025 ”. “It is well recognised by the international community that India lost more than a military conflict; it lost its credibility. Today, India can no longer import sympathy as it stands exposed in front of the world,” she said. “As stated by my prime minister, Pakistan remains steadfast in its pursuit of peace, mutual respect, dialogue and the peaceful settlement of disputes in our region and beyond — a commitment reflected in our consistent role as a peacemaker, mediator and bridge-builder,” she stated. “We will defend ourselves whenever aggression is imposed upon us, but we will never abandon the path to peace; for lasting strength lies not in the wars a nation can fight, but in the peace it has the courage to build and defend.” Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said any attempt by India to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of water would be treated as an “act of war”. Addressing the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, he said India’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance had no legal basis, adding that the country’s position had been rejected by UN experts and the Permanent Court of Arbitration.

Makkah alliance military chiefs vow to ‘immediately’ translate commitments into effective military cooperation: ISPR. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have expressed a shared determination to “immediately translate” their commitments under the Makkah Defence Alliance into effective military cooperation, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Saturday. The commitment was made at a meeting of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir and the chiefs of general staff of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in Riyadh on Friday. The meeting took place against the backdrop of heightened security concerns in the kingdom, with the Houthis and the Yemeni government engaged in renewed fighting . The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade targeting Saudi Arabia and attacked ships in the Red Sea, while also carrying out attacks in Saudi Arabia in recent weeks. Earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) had said the three countries were considering a meeting of their military chiefs to discuss ways to assist Riyadh under the Makkah Defence Alliance. According to the ISPR, the participants discussed measures to advance cooperation among their armed forces, including enhanced intelligence sharing, military coordination and integration of capabilities. The measures would help strengthen deterrence and collective defence, the military’s media wing said. The participants also reviewed the security situation and threats facing Saudi Arabia and strongly “resented” attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as well as civilian and economic infrastructure. They appreciated the vigilance and professionalism of the Saudi armed forces in ensuring the safety of the people and security of the kingdom, according to the ISPR. The military chiefs further affirmed their commitment to collective defence, which, the ISPR said, demonstrated the resolve of the three countries to defend Saudi Arabia’s security, sovereignty and territorial integrity. The ISPR added that the Riyadh meeting reflected the strength of the defence partnership among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, as well as their shared determination to implement the commitments under the tripartite defence agreement. The participants also commended the longstanding relations and mutual trust between the three countries and their armed forces. Kingdom ‘welcomed’ outcomes of meeting Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, in a post on X, said that he and CDF Field Marshal Munir “welcomed the outcomes” of the chiefs of staff meeting held under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. Prince Khalid said they discussed the “heinous attacks” targeting the holy city of Makkah as well as on the kingdom’s civilian and economic infrastructure. He said the two sides affirmed their continued joint efforts to confront the attacks in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The Makkah alliance was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in Makkah on Aug 7 and the first meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee was subsequently held in Istanbul on Aug 31, where the three countries agreed to establish a permanent secretariat in Riyadh and decided that Pakistan would provide the secretary general for its first three-year term. Pakistan appointed retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood as the alliance’s first secretary general , taking another step towards putting the institutional structure of the pact in place. The earlier New York ministerial meeting indicated that the three governments wanted the military chiefs to examine practical options. Therefore, the Riyadh meeting was expected to begin that process, although any decision on specific deployments or military assistance would depend on the Saudi requirement and the agreement reached by the three sides. Turkiye has already signalled its willingness to address Saudi military requirements, with Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan saying last week that Ankara was ready to help with “military needs, especially on some technical issues”. Pakistan has also repeatedly affirmed its commitment to the agreement.

Virat Kohli says 2027 World Cup will be his last for India. Virat Kohli said next year’s 50-over World Cup would be his last for India, and he is ready to give his all to help lift the trophy. Kohli, the leading century-maker in ODIs with 54 hundreds, retired from T20 Internationals and Test cricket earlier and now represents India only in the 50-over format. The 37-year-old batter, who has scored 14,941 runs in One-day Internationals, second only to Sachin Tendulkar’s 18,426, won the World Cup on home soil in 2011 before suffering defeat in the 2023 final against Australia. The 2027 edition, to be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in October to November, will be Kohli’s fifth ODI World Cup. “For me, it’s the last World Cup I’m going to play for India,” Kohli told broadcaster JioStar on Saturday. “That is my motivation and, like, you know, to leave everything out there. And of course, the goal is absolutely to win the World Cup, and whatever it takes, I’m absolutely ready.” Kohli said the demands of a 50-over World Cup made it one of cricket’s toughest challenges, particularly with the tournament set to be played away from home. “The intensity of a 50-over World Cup is greater than anything. Because now, it’s about 10 games at a Twenty20 level of intensity,” he said. “But you are playing 2.5 T20 games in one day. And to maintain that intensity for 10 games in a big tournament and World Cup is a big deal. Also now, it’s in foreign conditions. It takes a lot out of you.” Former captain Rohit Sharma, who also plays only ODIs for India, said he remained fully motivated by the prospect of another World Cup campaign. “The thought will never cross my mind that the business I had is finished,” Rohit said. “As long as you’re playing, there is always something to look forward to. And I’m looking forward to the World Cup.” Kohli and Rohit were both named in India’s squad for the three-match ODI series against West Indies. The opening match will be played in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday.

India's election commission orders review of voter-roll changes. The Election Commission of India ordered a review of its voter-roll software on Saturday after a newspaper reported that its chief had been questioned by his deputies over changes to voter lists that excluded millions of voters. Opposition parties have claimed the lists have been manipulated to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission of India has said differences are normal in any institution, and that all its actions were lawful. The Indian Express newspaper reported this week that two election commissioners had raised questions or expressed concerns to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at least 14 times in 10 months, mostly in connection with the process of updating voters’ lists that began last year. Opposition parties and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have demanded Kumar’s resignation . The CJP said it would launch nationwide protests on October 2 if he did not quit by Saturday. The Commission said on Saturday that a committee led by a senior election official and including an independent technology expert would examine whether the software complied with election laws and rules. It also said local officials would visit voters flagged for discrepancies instead of routinely requiring them to appear at government offices.

KP CM Afridi open to dialogue with govt but warns against 'misadventure'. PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday struck a conciliatory tone, offering to resolve issues with the federal government through dialogue but warned that any “misadventure” could result in serious repercussions. The PTI had been gearing up for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan, who is currently incarcerated in Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail. However, CM Afridi announced a day ago that the march has been postponed to Oct 4. Speaking to journalists during an informal discussion at KP House, Afridi said that his party had agreed to postpone the march to try and find amicable solutions to the issues through dialogue. However, he warned that any “misadventure” could lead the situation to a point of no return. Moreover, Afridi said that the federal government had 52 days to consider these demands, claiming the Centre was seeking time to discuss the issues. “We are not an armed group”, he asserted. “We want issues resolved through dialogue. No one has refused to engage in a dialogue.” The KP CM insisted that the PTI’s demands were genuine, including allowing Imran medical treatment at a private hospital in Islamabad, as well as granting him access to his lawyers, relatives and the court-nominated 18 party members. CM Afridi stressed that he had approached courts and written to the federal government for permission to meet the jailed ex-premier, but was “forced” to announce the Islamabad march in August as concerns regarding Imran’s health persisted . Asked about speculations regarding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, the chief minister said his supporters will be “on the road on a 24-hour notice”. “They would not be able to afford my removal,” he contended. Asked if there was any likely successor in the event of his removal from his office, the KP CM replied that it would be Imran’s prerogative. Afridi had been elected as the chief minister in October 2025, after the PTI founder had told Ali Amin Gandapur to resign . The chief minister also criticised his counterpart in Punjab, Maryam Nawaz, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and others for allegedly singling out Pakhtuns, claiming that there was a “well-hatched conspiracy” to divide Pakistan. “We are patriotic Pakistanis, and we are peaceful people. We will not allow any conspiracy to succeed,” he said. Defending his performance as the chief minister, Afridi highlighted that his government met high revenue targets and provided resources to the police to fight terrorism in the province. The PTI leader also reiterated his criticism of the federal government’s current Afghanistan policy and its failure to overcome terrorism. Afridi recalled that he had presented his own plan to the country’s military and civilian leadership to restore peace in the province by re-engaging with the Taliban regime in Afghanistan, reopening the border and ending the distinction between the so-called “good and bad Taliban”. Soon after the decision to postpone the long march, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday invited Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mehmood Achakzai for direct talks, apparently in a bid to ensure political stability in the country. According to a source close to the prime minister, PM Shehbaz extended the invitation for dialogue, but no response had so far been received from the opposition leader. “Yes [the PM has invited Mr Achakzai], but nothing yet [from the opposition side],” the source said. A PTI spokesman conf­irmed that the opposition leader had received the prime minister’s invitation. Meanwhile, in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory, security measures and preparations to deal with any emergency situation remain in place despite the postponement of the march. Punjab had already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province until Oct 5 and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad for two months. The federal government has also approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab from Sept 20 to Oct 5. Governor asks PTI to call off march after DI Khan bombing KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi requested that the PTI call off the Islamabad march in the wake of a deadly suicide bombing in the province’s Dera Ismail Khan district, which left 12 dead and 30 injured. “Considering today’s tragic suicide attack in DI Khan and the overall law and order situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, I’d advise the CM [Sohail Afridi] and [PTI] leadership to unconditionally call off the long march,” he wrote on X. “Our people need a united front. At a time when our province is facing the devastating consequences of terrorism, we must stand together, shoulder to shoulder with our police and security forces, in this fight against terrorism,” Kundi added. He implored Afridi to put political differences aside and stand together as one. “Our people are paying the price in blood. They deserve solidarity, security and leadership focused on protecting their lives. This is the time to stand with KP, stand with our people and stand with those defending them,” he wrote. Info minister calls Afridi a ‘coward’ Meanwhile, Information Minister Tarar defended the Centre’s counterterrorism policy and slammed the KP chief minister for his stance on the issue. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside the prime minister’s coordinator for KP Ikhtiar Wali, Tarar said: “Sohail Khan Afridi has lost his credibility and does not fight terrorists. “Why do I call him a coward? This is the one party that is the TTP’s B-team and the TTA’s C-team,” he said, referring to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the Tehreek-i-Taliban Afghanistan. “He does not want to take ownership of operations against terrorists, nor does he believe in them. Nor has he done anything, because of cowardice,” Tarar added. He claimed that the PTI had become weaker than ever and lost its political standing, alleging that the party had links with terrorists and was reluctant to condemn militant activities. “You don’t want to fight terrorism, and you are finished on the political front as well.” The minister asserted, “Our policy is not cowardice. We say openly that terrorists will be eliminated completely.” Recognising the sacrifices made by the police and security forces, Tarar emphasised that the government was determined to completely eliminate terrorism. “In 2026, over 4,600 suicide attacks may have happened, over 400 people may have been killed and over 1,500 injured, but will the provincial government listen?” he said. Speaking about the PTI’s march, he contended, “They said they will come for the march at their own time […] You can claim it is your choice, but it is not your decision and it is not your march.” In an X post in the evening, seemingly in response to Tarar’s remarks, Afridi asserted that his party was fully prepared for the march. “Our workers are eager for a peaceful long march. In any emergency situation, hundreds of thousands of our workers will be on the streets within a 24-hour deadline,” the PTI leader said.

Pakistan open FIFA Asean Cup campaign with 4-0 defeat against Thailand. Pakistan opened their FIFA Asean Cup campaign with a 4-0 defeat to Thailand at Si Jalak Harupat Stadium in Bandung, Indonesia, on Saturday, as Teerasak Poeiphimai struck twice and an own goal compounded the Green Shirts’ chastening introduction to the tournament. Pakistan, ranked 198th in the world and competing as a guest side, defended in numbers during a cagey opening half hour. Mohibullah produced a brilliant interception, and Ali Raza made a superb sliding tackle as Nolberto Solano’s men restricted Thailand to long-range efforts, with goalkeeper Yousuf Butt making a fine save on the half-hour mark. Yousuf was powerless moments later, however, when he saved a header from Jude Soonsup-Bell only for Teerasak to tuck in the rebound and open the scoring in the 31st minute. Thailand’s second arrived ten minutes later after captain Abdullah Iqbal’s misplaced pass led to a quick burst that ended with Soonsup-Bell slamming home from close range. Thailand had the ball in the net again three minutes later, but the effort was ruled offside. Pakistan needed inspiration, and coach Nolberto Solano made three substitutions at halftime, with Shayek Dost, Hayyan Khattak and Alamgir Ghazi coming on for Ali Raza, Ali Agha and Abdullah Shah. The changes brought more enterprise, with full-backs Mohammad Fazal and Haris Zeb making forward runs, and Pakistan started the second half brightly, keeping possession and threatening without making a decisive move. Thailand slowly grew back into the half and scored their third on the hour mark. Teerasak played a one-two with Supachai Chaided before his left-footed volley deflected off Haris Zeb and looped over goalkeeper Yousuf into the net. Abdul Samad Arshad attempted a curler from outside the box but missed the target as Pakistan tried to respond, and veteran Kaleemullah Khan was brought on with 19 minutes to go. At the 77th minute mark, Thailand missed a golden chance to extend their lead when a grounded cross came in from the left, but the forward completely missed the ball with only Yousuf to beat. Teerasak completed his brace six minutes from time. Pakistan failed to clear their lines, Peeradol Chamrasamee played the ball forward, and a smart touch from Kakana Khamyok played the forward onside. Teerasak placed the ball smartly past the goalkeeper to seal the victory. Solano’s side face the Philippines on Sept 29 before their final group-stage fixture against Vietnam on Oct 2. Pakistan entered the tournament on the back of winning the Diamond Jubilee International Football Tournament in the Maldives earlier this year, their first title in 74 years.

Naqvi assails PTI's 'version of equality before law' after KP IG told to ensure speaker's approval for any MPA's arrest. ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Saturday took strong exception to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government’s attempt to further solidify legislation mandating the assembly speaker’s prior permission for an MPA’s arrest or detention. In a post on X, Naqvi shared a KP Assembly Secretariat’s letter addressed to the KP inspector general (IG) on Friday, a day after the provincial cabinet approved the KP Police Act 2026. The proposed law, yet to be passed by the assembly, links the IG’s decisions to the chief minister or the government’s approval. In his letter to IG Zulfiqar Hameed, KP Assembly Deputy Secretary (Admin) Ibrahim Khan reminded him of Section 11 of the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act 2026 , which made the speaker’s approval mandatory to arrest or detain an MPA. The Act was among multiple pieces of legislation enacted in April by the KP government. A few of those provisions about lifetime blue passports and arms licences were withdrawn in August after facing criticism from the media and public. Commenting on the letter on Saturday, Naqvi said: “Now in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, even if an MPA is accused of a criminal offence, the police must first seek the speaker’s permission before arresting him. “What next?” the minister asked, detesting that in case an MPA killed a person, would the police “first wait for the speaker’s permission to arrest him?” “What an extraordinary version of ‘equality before law’. Well done. Keep it up! And this is Riyasat-i-Madina ?“ Naqvi wrote, referring to PTI founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan’s motto of transforming Pakistan into Riyasat-i-Madina (the State of Madina). In the letter, the KP Assembly Secretariat had directed the IG to ensure strict compliance with Section 11 of the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act, 2026. The letter reproduced the section, titled “permission of speaker before arrest, detention etc of a member”, which provides: “(1) When a member has to be arrested on a criminal charge or for a criminal offence or has to be detained under an executive order, the magistrate or the executive authority, as the case may be, shall seek prior permission of the speaker, indicating the reasons for the arrest or detention of the member in the appropriate form set out in the Second Schedule. “(2) Where the speaker deems it necessary in the public interest, he may require the relevant police officer to submit the police report or challan, as the case may be, to ascertain the facts of the matter. The speaker may, in his discretion, call up such inquiry before submission of challan in the court, as he may deem appropriate.” The KP Assembly Secretariat directed the IGP to ensure strict compliance with Section 11 and adopt the prescribed procedure before arresting or detaining any provincial lawmaker, whenever such action becomes necessary. A similar parliamentary rule introduced in October 2022 by PML-N mandates that police have to inform the National Assembly speaker before arresting any MNA. Responding to Naqvi on X, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati said : “If you had been part of an elected and people’s representative parliamentary system, you would have known that the protections given to Members of the Assembly are not a new invention; they have always been part of parliamentary traditions and national as well as provincial laws.” Swati explained that such laws “exist to protect the independence of the legislature, prevent the executive from using police powers to intimidate or silence elected representatives, and ensure that the assembly can function without fear or obstruction”. “They do not place any MPA above the law. An accused member remains subject to investigation, prosecution, and the full process of the courts.” Kundi wonders if PTI workers could get ‘same protection’ KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also commented on the KP law, questioning whether PTI workers would be given the “same protection that is now being demanded for their leaders”. “PTI workers should ask their leaders a very simple question: if they are pushed to the front lines of unlawful, criminal, anti-state activities, arrested, injured or prosecuted, will the speaker be answerable for them as well?” he wrote on X, sharing Naqvi’s post. “ Riyasat-i-Madina had leaders who submitted themselves to accountability. This looks more like leaders demanding immunity for themselves.” The fresh criticism comes amid an already heated debate over the new KP Police Act, with the interior ministry arguing that the provincial legislation violates the constitutional framework and weakens the police command structure at a time when KP remains on the frontline of the fight against terrorism. The approval came after the PTI claimed that dozens of its leaders and workers have been detained ahead of the party’s nationwide protest, now rescheduled for Oct 4 . It also said KP cabinet members were being targeted by unidentified individuals. During a cabinet meeting that approved the Police Act, CM Sohail Afridi said if his government was forcing the local bureaucracy, police, district commissioners or others to do anything wrong, then they should not obey those orders.

Trump rejects Iran's Hormuz plan, asserts US has imposed 'greatest blockade in military history'. Iran offered a plan to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz, Tehran said on Friday, but US President Donald Trump said he rejected the proposal. The waterway, key to the world’s oil supply, is central to the conflict between the United States and Iran, which is at a stalemate after nearly seven months . But new mediation efforts at the UN’s gathering of world leaders in New York this week offered some optimism of progress toward a deal. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met for talks on Tuesday with Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff, and previously set out conditions for ending the war and reopening the vital shipping channel. “Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days,” Araghchi said at the UN. “The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats, or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure.” However, Trump told reporters at the White House that “They (Iran) made a proposal, but I rejected it.” “They want to make a deal where they open the Strait immediately because they’re losing so badly,” he added. “They want to make a deal and I think that’s fine. I like making a deal too.” Trump added that Tehran was facing financial pressure, claiming that they made the proposal because “they are dying — the money isn’t coming in. “They got themselves into a bind; we have established the greatest blockade in military history — it’s a wall of steel. And now they have no money because they wanted to close the strait,” he added. Earlier today, The Wall Street Journal reported Trump had rejected the proposal, citing US officials familiar with the matter. The report noted that the 80-year-old president was sceptical Tehran would meet his demands and added he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely. Trump also posted an image to his Truth Social platform of a map showing the Strait of Hormuz circled and labelled “ Trump Strait .” Earlier media reports suggested the new plan calls for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East for seven days, including in Lebanon. Frozen assets It also reportedly calls for the release of frozen Iranian assets estimated to be worth at least $12 billion, as well as the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade of Iran. On the seventh day of the truce, Iran would reopen Hormuz. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in an interview with broadcaster CBS that the ceasefire “process will begin from the very day they accept it.” “We had previously reached an agreement based on the MOU that was signed in Pakistan … if the United States agrees to proceed in that way, everything will return to the way it was before,” he added. Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for the Revolutionary Guards, told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Tehran’s demands. The US and Iran signed a Pakistani-mediated memorandum of understanding in June that aimed to end the war, reopen the strait and launch talks on Iran’s nuclear programme. But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway. Iran requires ships to obtain authorisation before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons. Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the United States sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.

Suicide blast targeting DI Khan checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30. DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured on Saturday when a vehicle laden with explosives was rammed into the Aman Mela police checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan’s Darazinda tehsil, officials said. Separately, two rescue workers were killed and another was injured when a Rescue 1122 ambulance came under fire while transporting bodies of victims from the blast. DI Khan Regional Police Officer (RPO) Ghulam Mubashir Maken, citing an initial assessment, confirmed the casualties from the blast. He clarified that no law enforcement or security personnel were among the deceased, which included a Customs official and civilians. The deceased comprised nine men, two women and a minor. According to police and Rescue 1122 officials, an unidentified attacker rammed the explosives-laden tractor trolley into the checkpost. DI Khan District Police Officer (DPO) Ziauddin Ahmed confirmed that it was a suicide blast. The blast destroyed a large portion of the checkpost and completely demolished a house adjacent to the post. The intensity of the explosion was such that it was heard over a considerable distance, according to local officials and residents. Heavy firing was also heard following the blast. The Aman Mela checkpost, located near Mughal Kot and Darazinda on the DI Khan-Quetta Road, is used by police for security and checking along the route. It is situated close to the border between Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. According to RPO Maken, 25 of the injured were taken to the district headquarters (DHQ) hospital. Meanwhile, District Excise Officer Faheem Wazir said Excise personnel present at the checkpost remained safe. A bomb disposal team was also sent to the site to determine the nature of the explosion and examine the scene, police said. DPO Ahmed and the superintendent of police for the Saddar area had reached the site soon after the explosion and supervised the rescue operation. A Rescue 1122 spokesperson noted that their teams were on the site for relief operations, but mobile phone services were unavailable in the area. Later in the day, a Rescue 1122 spokesperson said the search, recovery and relief operation at the site had been completed. More than 25 personnel, six ambulances and a fire vehicle took part in the relief operations, according to the rescue service. On the directions of District Emergency Officer (DEO) Mohammad Arif Khan, four additional ambulances with staff were dispatched from DI Khan to assist in evacuating the injured. 2 killed as ambulance comes under fire Rescue 1122 said two of its workers were killed while another was seriously injured when an ambulance transporting some bodies recovered from the blast site was targeted by unidentified assailants near Aman Mela. The deceased rescue workers were identified as Sharifullah and Imtiaz, while Anees sustained injuries in the firing, according to a Rescue 1122 spokesperson. The injured worker was provided immediate medical treatment and taken to a hospital. Despite the firing incident, rescue teams had continued the operation to transport the bodies and assist those affected by the blast. State broadcaster Radio Pakistan attributed the attack to Fitna al Khawarij, a term the state uses to refer to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). The report added that an operation by the security forces against the terrorists was underway. ‘Political priorities must reflect the pain of our people’ Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, in a video statement , condemned the attack and highlighted the funds allocated for police in KP’s budget. He also once again called for a “policy shift” on the federal government’s part regarding counterterrorism. Terrorists, their facilitators, financiers and sponsors will be held accountable and no territory beyond our borders will be allowed to serve as a sanctuary for terrorism against Pakistan,” he said. “We will neither be intimidated nor divided. Pakistan will prevail,” Bilawal said. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb also condemned the blast at the “Customs joint check post”. Rise in terrorism KP has witnessed an increase in terrorist activity in recent months, with law enforcement agencies and security forces being targeted, prompting authorities to intensify counterterrorism operations. IHC voids law allowing agencies to curb travel. ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has declared unconstitutional a provision of the Passport Rules, 2021, that allowed the placement of a citizen’s name on the Passport Control List (PCL) on the recommendation of government agencies or departments without identifying a competent authority or providing legal safeguards. Justice Raja Inaam Ameen Minhas, in a detailed judgement, declared the second limb of Rule 22(2)(b) ultra vires the Passports Act, 1974, and Articles 4, 9, 10A and 15 of the Constitution, holding that it was of no legal effect. The judgement was issued on a petition filed by Moinuddin, who was offloaded at Islamabad International Airport on Dec 18, 2025, while travelling to Saudi Arabia for Umrah. He possessed a valid Pakistani passport, a valid Saudi visa and a confirmed air ticket, but no reason was communicated to him for stopping him from travelling. The court noted that his passport had never been impounded, confiscated, cancelled or inactivated, nor had its issuance or renewal been refused. The dispute, therefore, centred on the question whether the agency had the authority to restrain a citizen from travelling on a valid passport. According to the judgement, his name was placed on the PCL on Dec 24, 2024, on the recommendation of NCB-INTERPOL, forwarded by the FIA’s Assistant Director (Immigration Wing). The action followed his deportation from the UK after his conviction for causing death by dangerous driving while under the influence of alcohol. He had served a three-year sentence. The court noted that he had completed his sentence and been deported, while no criminal case, inquiry or investigation was pending against him in Pakistan. He was neither a proclaimed offender nor the subject of an extradition request. The IHC rejected the justification provided by the passport authorities to retain his name on the PCL that his conduct had adversely affected Pakistan’s reputation and that the placement was intended to create deterrence. The court observed that these grounds were not contained in the Passports Act or the Passport Rules. Rule 21 dealt with refusal of a passport and did not authorise restraint of a citizen who already possessed a valid passport, the judgement stated. “The refusal of a passport and the prohibition of travel are two separate exercises of power,” Justice Minhas observed, declaring that the function of the relevant division and directorate general to “prepare and maintain” the PCL was administrative and did not itself confer jurisdiction to decide whose name could be placed on the list. The court pointed out that Rule 22(2) referred to individuals whose passport facilities had been refused. Moinuddin had never been refused a passport. It also noted that Rule 22(2)(a) specifically identified the additional secretary of the relevant division as the authority competent to place and remove names in Category A, whereas clause (b) identified no such authority. The IHC held that neither the directorate general of FIA nor NCB-INTERPOL possessed the authority to place the petitioner’s name on the PCL in the circumstances of the case. It observed that the impugned order merely stated that it had been issued with the approval of the “competent authority” without identifying that authority, the legal provision invoked or the material on which the decision was based. The court found that the impugned provision provided no competent authority, objective criteria, notice, hearing, reasons or communication of the decision, meaning that a citizen could learn of the restriction only after being stopped at the immigration counter. The judgement declared the second limb of Rule 22(2)(b) — allowing PCL placement on the recommendations of government agencies or departments — beyond Sections 8 and 13 of the Passports Act and inconsistent with the Constitution. About the reasons of “international reputation” and “deterrence”, the court held that since the petitioner had completed his sentence and no proceedings were pending against him, the restraint had no “live and proximate nexus with a present necessity”. “Gravity does not supply jurisdiction,” it said. Expressing displeasure over the authorities’ failure to comply with an earlier order, the IHC directed them to decide the petitioner’s application within one week through a speaking and well-reasoned order. The court consequently set aside the Jan 26, 2026, order of the agency and declared the petitioner’s placement on the PCL on Dec 24, 2024, without lawful authority and of no legal effect. It directed the authorities to remove his name from the PCL within 15 days of receiving a certified copy of the judgement and not to interfere with his lawful foreign travel on the basis of the impugned placement. The court clarified that the competent authority could still take action warranted by law after following the prescribed procedure. Copies of the judgement were sent to the Interior Secretary, Immigration and Passports DG and FIA DG for compliance. Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026
